title: move_failed concentrates early and near spawn/edges
detail: REFUTED: the ~50% failures were not spawn/edge proximity. Root cause was a pathfinder bug (routing onto solid 'frontier' walls) plus stepping onto monster tiles. Fixed in explorer/0.2.0; see 'BUG (fixed): pathfinder routed onto solid frontier walls'.

title: First improvement: smarter movement fallback to cut move_failed
detail: Shipped in explorer/0.2.0 (nav wall-frontier fix + monster-tile blocking + destination reservation). Confirmed: move_failed 55%->0.8%.

detail: vale=brewing, mines=forging, spire=magic. Once each world's ingredient/flux/recipe vocabulary is known, consider dedicating parties to each map's crafting pillar rather than uniform exploring.

title: explorer/0.1.0: ~50% of moves fail (move_failed) and drive stamina exhaustion
detail: Over a ~10.8k-tick live window: move_failed=19276 vs move=18742 (~half fail); action_error_rate 9.9% dominated by not_enough_stamina=3185. Failed moves still cost stamina, cascading into unaffordable-action errors.
evidence: guild_log.db run #2 @ tick ~10791: events move/move_failed, action_errors GROUP BY reason.

title: Monster tiles block movement but baseline paths onto them
detail: The baseline keeps monster tiles walkable (to attack on contact) and does not add them to the pathing blocked-set, so it steps onto monsters and bounces (move_failed) whenever a monster sits on a path but is not the current adjacency-attack target.
test: explorer/0.2.0 blocks monster tiles in pathing (attack when adjacent, route around otherwise); expect move_failed rate to drop sharply in the next window. Falsified if move_failed stays ~50% after the change.

title: BUG (fixed): pathfinder routed onto solid "frontier" walls
detail: nav.bfs_step allowed stepping onto a GOAL tile even if it was a known-solid wall; nav.frontier counted a wall bordering the unseen as an exploration target. So the explorer repeatedly targeted wall tiles and walked into them -> move_failed. Likely a major share of the ~50% failed-move rate. Fixed: goal special-case now excludes known-solid tiles; frontier requires a standable tile. Surfaced by mutation-checking the destination-reservation test.
evidence: Reproduced in a unit scenario: bfs_step onto a wall goal returned a step; now returns None. tests/test_nav.py covers it.

title: UI: metric time-series graphs with per-version overlay
detail: Line charts of gold/hr, xp/hr, deaths, move_failed rate and action-error rate over ticks, with run-window (version) bands/overlays so a deploy s before/after is visible at a glance. Directly supports the loop s own measurement. Likely the next UI build.

title: UI: map heatmaps (deaths, loot density, move_failed hotspots)
detail: Overlay toggles on the pan/zoom map: where characters die, where loot/gold concentrates, and where moves bounce — practical for spotting bad terrain/pathing and fun to watch accumulate.

title: UI: live roster panel — what each character is doing now
detail: A per-character strip (hp/stamina/carry, current world+pos, last chosen action + one-line reasoning), updating live, so the guild is legible at a glance without scrolling the decision feed.

title: Death diagnosis: died-on-arrival on spire, poisoned, no stamina to flee
detail: 306 char-deaths/984 recruits=0.31; 74% on spire (hardest map) but shallow (median y12) and fast (76% within ~200 ticks of embark); ~22% HP at death; 35% actively poisoned; 45% of hurt-decisions rested (couldn't afford the step home). Fix: run_id/grouping indexes (SCHEMA + applied live), O(1) gold-delta (first+last village frame), and a ~3s TTL cache in the UI. 25s->1.78s cold / ~1.5ms warm.
evidence: RCA subagent timings: _run_summaries 16.8s of 18.3s; per-run COUNT frames 7.3s, gold-delta blob fetch 7.9s + decompress 2.25s; after fix snapshot 1.57s local / 1.78s cold via UI.

Materialize a small per-run summary (gold first/last, counts) at run close, THEN prune old raw frames. Not urgent for speed (indexes make snapshot fast at any size); it's a disk concern.

evidence: actions_sent equip=1 (run7) + 'equip' event=1; field sample ~10% hand-equipped, 0% outfit.

Don't let equipping a weak tool (pickaxe) block acquiring a proper weapon. Body armor comes only from loot, so keep looted 'outfit' gear and equip it.

detail: Seen: 184 herb + 165 crop + 47 ore-vein + 58 track tiles, chests/safes, 4 portals, 1 cauldron. detail: Buy/loot tomes (tome_veil 120, tome_bolt 150) to learn forms; attune essences via focus ingredients from brewing; map the per-world weave circle by reading resound/fray. clarity purges hostile workings (poison!), vigor mends (heal). This is the spire's pillar and the direct counter to the status_damage that now dominates deaths.

detail: run #8: 6 brewed (potion_red x5, potion_gold x1) / 6 failed (murky, curdled) = 50%. Tells: dark_sheen(5), pale_crust(2), acrid_smoke(1), sweet_mist(1). brew_started carries only a timer (ticks:10); ingredient correlation must come from the brew action's item_ids + inventory.

evidence: run #8 (git a44958d), 34 mapped brews; all 7 curdles were vigor+venom pairs

detail: Circle axis: vigor <-> venom are directly opposed (all 7 observed curdles were vigor+venom, nothing else). Confirmed: bone=vigor, venom_sac=venom, ectoplasm=aether (fixed calibration); embercap=VIGOR (HIGH; 'ember' name is a red herring); moonbell=VENOM (HIGH); potion_red re-brews as vigor. Off-axis (ember/frost/clarity/aether), partially placed: glimmerweed ~adjacent venom, bitterroot ~adjacent vigor, fickle_pearl likely aether (blink_dust), frostmoss + sungrass distance-2 (unplaced).

evidence: run #8, product frequencies vs ingredient sets across 34 brews
title: Brew product -> essence/effect (this world)
detail: potion_red=vigor/heal (HIGH); flask_green=venom majority (HIGH); vial_green=venom combine (glimmerweed+venom_sac); potion_gold=vigor combine (bitterroot+embercap); flask_orange=frostmoss's off-axis essence; blink_dust~aether (glimmerweed+fickle_pearl, 'blink'). Higher tier from more/agreeing ingredients.

evidence: run #8 tell frequencies per ingredient across 34 brews
title: Tells are per-INGREDIENT: pale_crust=sungrass/frostmoss, sweet_mist=bitterroot, dark_sheen=noise
detail: pale_crust -> sungrass(9/9)/frostmoss(7/8); sweet_mist -> bitterroot(7/7)+fickle_pearl; acrid_smoke -> embercap/moonbell/potion_blue; dark_sheen fires on 32/34 brews (near-universal) => treat as NOISE, not diagnostic.

title: Iteration next: essence-AWARE brewing (stop curdling; target vigor healing)
detail: Blind brewing curdles ~50% by mixing vigor+venom. Encode the learned essence map as DATA the strategy reads (not hardcoded logic), brew SAME-essence groups (never mix vigor+venom), and target vigor (bone/embercap/potion_red) for reliable potion_red healing at higher tier. Also `taste` unknown off-axis herbs to complete the map. Dual-use: essence knowledge feeds M4 magic attunement (focus ingredients).

title: Watch: essence-aware brewing may strand minority-essence herbs
detail: _should_sell keeps all `brew` items, and _choose_brew only brews same-essence batches of >=2. A char carrying e.g. 1 vigor + 1 venom herb can now brew NEITHER (declining to curdle) and won't sell them -> they occupy carry cap and can trip the 'pack full -> go home' branch. Watch carry-full frequency + un-brewable-herb accumulation next window; if it regresses, add: sell the excess of the minority essence once a same-essence batch has been brewed. [CONFIRMED run #9: held 0.49->1.83, full-carry 0%->14.5%, move/stamina errors 7.5%->17.7%. FIXED in v0.8.0: stranded brewables are now sold, not hoarded.]

evidence: run #9: 3 brew_failed events, 2 'curdled' + 1 'murky', all with the pale_crust tell (=> an undecoded off-axis herb present); no decoded vigor/venom batch curdled
title: Undecoded off-axis herbs are NOT all one essence — blind-mixing them curdles
detail: The off-axis herbs (sungrass/frostmoss/glimmerweed/bitterroot/fickle_pearl) span multiple essences (ember/frost/clarity/aether), so v0.7.0's 'brew all-unknown herbs together' learning batch conflicts and curdles. 'curdled' == essence conflict by definition, so this confirms >=2 distinct essences among the undecoded set. Clean single-essence brewing of the DECODED herbs (vigor->potion_red, venom->flask_green) succeeded in the same window.

title: v0.8.0: learn undecoded herbs by taste / same-KIND brew, not blind-mixed batches
detail: v0.7.0 learns unknowns by mixing them, which curdles (wastes ingredients) and doesn't cleanly attribute an essence. Refine: for undecoded ingredients, prefer (a) `taste` a single herb (destructive but definitive -> essence directly), or (b) a batch of >=2 of the SAME kind (cannot curdle -> product reveals that kind's essence). This completes this world's essence map with far less waste and feeds M4 magic attunement (focus ingredients need known essences). Also record potion_blue/potion_yellow as new products to place. [v0.8.0 shipped the same-KIND-batch half (no more mixed-unknown curdles). The `taste`-to-learn half is deferred to v0.9.0 — see the new consideration.]

evidence: sampled 400 field frames/run: run#8 avg_brew_held=0.49 full=0.0%; run#9 avg_brew_held=1.83 full=14.5%; not_enough_stamina/move 7.5%->17.7% of actions
title: Hoarding un-brewable ingredients fills carry and stalls chars (move/stamina errors)
detail: Brew ingredients kept but never brewable accumulate in inventory, fill carry cap, and make chars repeatedly attempt (and fail on stamina) to walk home to sell. The lever is to SELL what can't be brewed. Generalizes: any 'keep for later' item class needs a drain, or it becomes carry debt.  UPDATE (0.9.0 analysis): 0.8.0's sell-stranded fix addressed the carry driver; the RESIDUAL 0.8.0 move/not_enough_stamina is NOT carry (carry was low ~2/24 at the failures) but ~1-tick FRAME STALENESS on plain-floor moves — see the staleness conjecture and the 0.9.0 headroom fix.

title: Deferred: taste stranded undecoded singletons instead of selling them
detail: v0.8.0 sells undecoded singletons (unclogs carry) but that discards a learning opportunity: `taste` a lone undecoded herb (destructive, definitive -> its essence directly) before selling. DEFERRED past 0.9.0: the analyze milestone read put the M1 action-error regression (~0.5) ahead of M3 crafting, so 0.9.0 shipped the field-move stamina fix instead. Revisit once competence is restored.

evidence: run #9 stopped_at stayed NULL after run #10 (0.8.0) superseded it during hot-redeploy
title: Hot-redeploy hard-kills the outgoing runner, so end_run() is skipped
detail: The zero-downtime handoff supersedes the old session server-side and the supervisor swap kills the old process before its kick handler/end_run runs. Any cleanup that must happen on the OLD runner's shutdown is unreliable; make the NEW runner responsible instead (begin_run now closes dangling windows). Same lesson applies to any future 'flush on shutdown' logic.

title: Long-open run isn't archived — rotate run window (or age-based partial archival)
detail: tools/archive_frames.py archives whole CLOSED runs older than 48h. If the improvement loop pauses (usage cap) the current run stays open indefinitely and its frames never age out -> unbounded growth for that one run, defeating retention on a true walk-away. Fix options: (a) runner rotates its run window on a timer (close+reopen every ~24h) so closed archivable runs are always produced; metrics aggregate by strategy_version across windows. (b) archive+prune frames by AGE from the open run too (partial-run archives; manifest becomes multi-chunk per run). (a) is simpler and keeps the whole-run archive model. Do before any extended unattended period.

title: Village economy actions cost NO stamina (never fail not_enough_stamina)
detail: sell/buy/brew/equip/spend_xp are free of stamina cost, so gating them cannot reduce not_enough_stamina. Refutes advice.md's #1 'stamina-gate the village loop' as a no-op.
evidence: action_errors over ALL history: sell/buy/brew/equip/spend_xp appear only with no_such_item / not_enough_xp / wrong_slot / not_enough_gold / crafting / not_in_village — ZERO not_enough_stamina rows.

title: not_enough_stamina is 98% field `move`; failures are frame staleness, not terrain/cost
detail: The stamina leak is entirely field-side movement, not the village and not cost underestimation on floor. Floor move cost is 20 and the gate already checks >=20, yet moves are rejected — because the acted-on frame is ~1 tick stale (shown stamina > server's live).
evidence: 0.8.0 window: not_enough_stamina by action = move 83,361 vs attack 1,042. Measured floor move cost = 20 (successful-move stamina drop 14/15 + regen 5/6). Failed moves cluster at SHOWN stamina 13-29 (median 23, p95 28) on 94% plain floor; web/rime = 0% of failures.

title: The bot decides on ~1-tick-stale frames (shown stamina > server's live value)
detail: Explains move not_enough_stamina at shown-sta well above the true cost on plain floor. The 0.9.0 headroom (1.5x move cost) is a decision-layer mitigation; the deeper cause is client-layer frame freshness. RESOLVED (0.9.0 window): the 1.5x headroom cut move/not_enough_stamina 3-6x on the long sqlite run #22 (~0.50 -> 0.078); the falsification (move not_enough_stamina stays high) did NOT fire. Staleness confirmed as the mechanism, headroom as the mitigation.
test: If 0.9.0's headroom sharply cuts move/not_enough_stamina next window, staleness is confirmed as the mechanism (terrain and base-cost already ruled out). REFUTED if move not_enough_stamina stays high despite the headroom. Deeper fix to try then: decide only on the latest frame per world, dropping stale queued frames.

title: v0.9.0: stamina headroom (1.5x) on field moves to end the not_enough_stamina retry-storm
detail: offer() now requires stamina >= 1.5x raw cost for move/ride (MOVE_STAMINA_SAFETY); attack/use/etc. stay at raw cost. Deployed on run #15 (sqlite). Mutation-checked tests in tests/test_decision_engine.py.

title: MariaDB backend seam: schema splitter truncated the decisions DDL on a ';' in a comment
detail: apply_schema crash-looped any MariaDB-backed runner at Storage() init: _split_statements split the DDL on a ';' living inside a `--` comment in the decisions CREATE TABLE, handing the driver a truncated statement (1064). Fixed (be184e6) by stripping `--` comments before splitting. MariaDB migration now unblocked; live prod still on sqlite by choice.
evidence: Reproduced statement-by-statement against the live MariaDB (statements 5+6 failed). After the fix, apply_schema applies all 7 tables cleanly and STEEMER_TEST_MARIADB=1 test_mariadb_roundtrip passes end-to-end.

title: redeploy.sh daemon-detach does not survive the Claude-Code harness; host supervisor in screen/tmux
detail: Both `daemon -f` supervisor trees launched via a Claude Bash tool call vanished within minutes; the operator's screen-hosted make run-live lived 4h. For the autonomous loop to redeploy durably under Claude, launch run-live.sh inside a persistent screen/tmux session (done for 0.9.0 run #15) or give daemon a supervise+pidfile setup that escapes the harness reaper.

title: Next target after 0.9.0: phantom-character error family (no_such + unknown + not_in_village = 52%)
detail: SHIPPED as explorer/0.10.0. Diagnosis corrected: NOT rival players (all failing uids are our own guild g_cd0e2a) and NOT mainly 'a char the frame no longer holds' — it is a DUPLICATE-SEND STORM. village() re-issued the SAME embark/recruit every tick on a ~few-tick-stale frame (the just-commanded char still shows in chars_here), so 98% of embarks were same-char re-sends within 8 ticks; the tail bounced no_such_character (294) / roster_cap (48). Fix: in-flight guard (EMBARK/RECRUIT_COOLDOWN) + count in-flight embarks toward world_cap. The field move/attack unknown_character remainder is a DIFFERENT mechanism (server lag echoing moves queued for a char that died mid-field) and is not bot-fixable from the frame.

title: MariaDB sustains live play; a 'stall' was a REPEATABLE-READ monitoring artifact
detail: Live writes are ~25 ms/frame (frame blob 4.4 ms + 150-400 tile upserts ~15 ms + plain-INSERT executemany), under the ~62 ms frame budget — so NO async queue / Valkey / writer-thread is needed; synchronous writes keep up. The apparent 'stall after ~1000 frames' was NOT real: a reused db.connect() (autocommit=False) held an InnoDB REPEATABLE READ snapshot, so repeated COUNT(*) never advanced. ALWAYS monitor live MariaDB progress with a FRESH connection (or autocommit / READ COMMITTED) per sample.  FIXED IN CODE (0.10.0): connect(readonly=True) on MariaDB was a documented no-op (autocommit=False, InnoDB default REPEATABLE READ), so any reader that outlived its first SELECT froze an MVCC snapshot for the connection's life — the real code-level cause of the 'stall/gated reads'. connect() now opens readonly connections autocommit=True under READ COMMITTED so each SELECT is a fresh snapshot; regression test in tests/test_mariadb_roundtrip.py (live-verified + mutation-checked).
evidence: Killed runs #24/#25 actually reached 3024 / 1865 frames (ticks 411962 / 413060) per fresh-connection queries; benchmark: 200-tile executemany upsert = 15 ms, frame insert = 4.4 ms.

title: export_run buffered a whole run on MariaDB; fixed with a streaming (unbuffered) cursor
detail: The seam's default cursor is buffered on MariaDB, so archive export materialised an entire run in memory — unsafe as prune only runs after a verified archive (disk fills at ~7 GiB/day). Added Connection.execute_stream (unbuffered on MariaDB) and used it in export_run.
evidence: Real 9,480-frame run exports at 3 MB peak RSS (flat = streaming). Committed 66e2732; unit guard + live roundtrip export test green.

title: Cut the live bot over to MariaDB as source of truth (no more --db sqlite shim)
detail: config.toml=mariadb is now live truth; bare `make run-live` is correct. sqlite guild_log.db (6.3 GB) kept as a cold backup and a selectable backend. Run #27 live, screen-hosted. Retention archives from MariaDB via the streaming export fix.

title: Phantom-character family is a duplicate-send storm on stale village frames (not rival players)
detail: 0.9.0 MariaDB window: no_such_character+unknown_character+not_in_village ~60% of live errors. Two distinct mechanisms, both our own guild (uids g_cd0e2a_*): (1) VILLAGE embark/recruit re-sent every tick because the frame is a few ticks stale (just-commanded char still in chars_here) — run #28 sent 3135 embarks for ~28 chars, 294 bounced no_such_character, and a replay measured 3151/3201 embarks were same-char re-sends within 8 ticks. (2) FIELD move/attack unknown_character is the server's LAGGING echo of moves queued for a char that died mid-field: char c7494's 53 moves (ticks 419946-420000, alive) drew 33 unknown_character errors at ticks 420004-420118, all AFTER the bot stopped sending (char had left every frame). Mechanism (2) is not bot-fixable from the frame; (1) is fixed by the 0.10.0 in-flight guard.
evidence: per-run x per-reason query on explorer/0.9.0; actions_sent vs action_errors correlation for c7494/c7500; replay of run-28 village frames through 0.10.0 (0 same-char re-embarks vs 3151 in a 0.9.0 sim).

title: ore_copper/ore_iron are smeltable (uses=['smelt']); the guild looted ore and SOLD it
detail: Item model (sqlite inventory scan): ore_copper & ore_iron carry uses=['smelt']; lumber & gem_rough carry uses=['forge']. Sale events show the guild sold 316 ore_copper, 66 ore_iron, 195 lumber, 38 pickaxe. So the M3a feedstock is already being looted (no mining of vein tiles required to start). explorer/0.10.0 now smelts a matching ore pair into an ingot in the village (smelt takes only item_ids, needs no vocabulary), keeping paired ore and selling only stranded singles (the v0.8.0 anti-clog rule). smelt reduces carry (2->1).
evidence: sqlite frames inventory scan (uses per kind); events sale/buy kind histogram.

title: forge is blocked on unpublished per-world `product` vocabulary — deferred, not shippable blind
detail: forge {product, item_ids} REQUIRES a product NAME, and there are ZERO `forged` events in all recorded history, so no product name is confirmed. Unlike brewing — where the pot infers the product from majority essence, so a blind brew never earns an action error (only curdles, a quality failure) — a guessed forge product is an unknown_* ACTION error, the exact class 0.10.0 is reducing. So blind-forge is NOT the analog of the v0.6.0 blind-brew foundation. 0.10.0 ships smelt (banks ingots + logs metal tells); forge lands once a product name is learned.
evidence: docs/03-actions.md & docs/07-crafting.md (forge needs `product`); events table has no `forged`/`smelt` kind across all history.

title: BUG (fixed 0.10.0): readonly MariaDB connections pinned a REPEATABLE-READ snapshot
detail: steemer/db.py connect(readonly=True) opened MariaDB autocommit=False with no isolation override, so InnoDB's default REPEATABLE READ applied and the connection's first SELECT froze an MVCC snapshot for its whole life; `readonly` was a documented no-op. Any reader held across samples (a monitor, the analysis tool kept open) never saw the running bot's new frames and read as 'stalled/gated', and left an open txn pinning a metadata lock + undo history. Fix: readonly connections now open autocommit=True under READ COMMITTED, so each SELECT is a fresh statement-consistent read. This is the code-level fix the earlier 'monitoring artifact' note only worked around by habit.
evidence: live probe: readonly conn reported REPEATABLE-READ/autocommit=0; regression test test_readonly_connection_sees_writes_committed_after_its_first_read (live-verified pass, mutation-checked: reverting connect() makes it read 0 instead of 1).

title: v0.10.0: embark/recruit in-flight guard + M3a smelt (ore->ingot)
detail: Guard: track tick each char embarked / each recruit; skip re-sending while in-flight (EMBARK/RECRUIT_COOLDOWN=8), count in-flight embarks toward world_cap. Smelt: pair matching ore -> ingot in the village, keep paired ore (sell stranded singles). Mutation-checked tests in tests/test_decision_engine.py. Deployed on the MariaDB backend.

title: The 0.10.0 in-flight guard cuts the phantom (no_such_character + roster_cap) share next window
detail: Baseline to beat (explorer/0.9.0 per-run errors): run#28 no_such_character 264 + roster_cap 48 + not_in_village 81; runs #24/#25/#27 similar (no_such 409/240/162, unknown 206/174/210). Replay predicts embark same-char re-sends 3151->0.
test: REFUTED if next window's (no_such_character + roster_cap) per-1k-frames rate does NOT fall vs the #24/#25/#27/#28 baseline. The field unknown_character rate is expected to be roughly UNCHANGED (server-lag death-echo, not addressed) — so the fall should concentrate in the embark/recruit reasons, not move/attack.

title: M3a forge: wire once a `product` name is learned (needs a non-storming discovery path)
detail: 0.10.0 banks ingots but does not forge (no confirmed product name). To land forge without an unknown_product storm: harvest a product name from an observed forged event (another guild forging in a shared world), the shop, or an operator-supplied name; then forge {product, [ingot(,lumber for hafted)(,gem_rough as flux)]} and learn the per-metal flux from the `forged` tells. Keep ingots+lumber+gem_rough (stop selling) once forge fires.

title: Optional: read shop.stock[].req to pick a buyable weapon data-drivenly
detail: Upstream starter kit (d18214c) exposes a per-kind `req` stat-requirement dict on frame.shop.stock entries and its example bots now read it instead of hard-coding str>=4. steemer still hard-codes 'shortsword if str>=4 else club' (explorer.py). Not a bug (the buy is legal; an over-strong weapon is caught by the stat_requirement equip error), but reading `req` would future-proof weapon choice against a shortsword whose requirement changes or involves another stat. Low priority.

title: Village-frame guild snapshot (chars_here + chars_by_world) undercounts the true live roster
detail: Operator noticed our UI roster (7 = 5 home + 2 fielded) vs the server's own map (28). Investigated run #32: the reported roster (home + fielded, read from the latest village frame's guild snapshot) SWINGS 30->6->30 over ~2400 ticks, but only 5 death events occurred during the 30->6 drop and just 13 recruits all run — so the guild snapshot is NOT tracking real churn; it is a lagged/partial view that momentarily drops live chars (in-transit during rapid embark waves, and worlds its chars_by_world doesn't currently list even though a char is on them). Our per-frame data is internally consistent (village chars_by_world matches the current field frames), so the undercount is in the SERVER's village guild-snapshot cadence, not our parsing. The reliable roster count is DISTINCT live char_uids across a recent window of ALL world frames (=30), not any single village frame. STRATEGY RISK: village() computes roster=len(here)+fielded and fielded from this same snapshot to gate recruit (roster<cap) and embark (fielded+inflight<world_cap) — so an undercount can over-recruit / over-deploy. The UI (metrics.snapshot -> _latest_frame('village')) faithfully shows the dips because it reconnects per refresh (NOT pinned; today's readonly-snapshot fix is unrelated to this). DEEPER ROOT CAUSE (investigated further): the server presents chars INTERMITTENTLY — a live char is absent from ALL received frames for up to ~350 ticks (median max sighting gap 342t among long-lived chars in run #32), and the guild's true roster is LARGE and PERSISTENT across runs (uids up to c7615, far more than the ~13 recruit events this run). So the frame's guild snapshot is an inherently PARTIAL view of a big persistent roster; the 'server map shows 28, our UI shows 7' gap is that the server's map knows the full roster while frames only carry the currently-loaded subset. CONSEQUENCE: the true roster CANNOT be reliably reconstructed from frames — a RosterTracker over any window fails (30t: no change to the dip; 800t: stdev only 6.6->5.6, and dead chars then linger 800t). So a strategy 'fix' to gate recruit/embark on a reconstructed count is NOT achievable and was NOT shipped; 0.10.0's recruit cooldown already curbs the over-recruit (roster_cap 87->11 in run #32). The achievable wins are OBSERVABILITY: an honest UI roster panel (snapshot + recent range + frame age) and a low-noise anomaly on action-error spikes / roster_cap rejections — NOT a reconstructed-count fix.
evidence: run #32: roster trajectory from village frames (30,26,22,20,15,13,8,6,9,25,30) vs 5 deaths + 13 recruits; distinct own uids over last ~50 ticks = 30 while a low village frame reported 6.

title: Shipped: low-noise action-error-spike anomaly self-reporting + honest roster/inventory dashboard panel
detail: Response to the roster-desync finding: since the true roster can't be reconstructed from frames, ship observability instead of a false-precision fix. (1) steemer/anomaly.py AnomalyMonitor flags a spiking action-error family (>=80 in a 300-tick window, re-report >=1200 ticks) to stdout + bot_anomaly events (shown on the dashboard via anomalies_recent; the bot does NOT write findings.jsonl directly) (7 flags/run #28, 11/run #32 — pinpoints the chronic unknown_character death-echo, quiet on a healthy stream). (2) metrics.snapshot gained roster{home,by_world,total,range,frame_age_s,inventory} + anomalies_recent; UI panel shows total-as-now + recent range + frame age + a partial-view note so a dip reads as transient. Strategy unchanged (explorer/0.10.0). Prototype RosterTracker/reconcile for gating the strategy was REVERTED (no window reliably reconstructs the count; 0.10.0's recruit cooldown already curbs over-recruit).

title: BUG (fixed): snapshot MIN/MAX(received_at) full-scanned frames (~38s of a ~50s live snapshot)
detail: While adding the roster panel I found metrics.snapshot() takes ~50s on the live MariaDB. Instrumented it: SELECT MIN(received_at) and MAX(received_at) FROM frames were ~19s EACH — received_at is an unindexed double, so each full-scans the large frames table. (My roster/inventory + anomalies_recent additions are ~0.1s, not the cause.) received_at is written monotonically with the autoincrement seq PK, so first/last-by-seq give the same wall span via an index-only PK lookup. Fixed: SELECT received_at FROM frames ORDER BY seq ASC/DESC LIMIT 1. Snapshot 49.7s -> 11.9s, identical result. Same class as finding [19]'s dependent-subquery fix in _run_gold_delta; received_at was the one MIN/MAX left unindexed. Residual ~12s is COUNT(*)/GROUP-BY over the big tables + _run_summaries (~8s over ~30 runs) — acceptable for a background-published snapshot, left for later.
evidence: inline per-statement timing of snapshot() on live MariaDB: min_received 18.9s, max_received 18.7s; after the seq-order rewrite the full snapshot dropped 49.7s->11.9s with wall_seconds unchanged.

title: /api/spectate/guilds (public HTTP) gives the AUTHORITATIVE roster the ZeroMQ frames don't
detail: Scanned the vendored server web client (reference_web/app.js). GET https://bot.willmorrison.net/api/spectate/guilds (public, no auth) returns {tick, maps, guilds:[{guild_id, name, characters, roster:[{char_uid,name,level,world,look,equipment}], color}]}. `characters` is the true total roster count and each roster entry carries its current `world` — the authoritative count + per-world distribution that the village frame's chars_here/chars_by_world only partially/laggingly show (the '7 vs 28' desync). Live check: our guild g_cd0e2a shows characters=16, by_world={vale:5,village:11}. So the STRATEGY roster-accounting fix I concluded was impossible from frames IS achievable by polling this endpoint (cache ~30-60s, non-blocking, fall back to the frame snapshot on error). Also confirms MULTIPLAYER: a rival guild g_63837f 'WillMorr' (characters=25) is present — the 'first new guild' the operator noted. Vendored at reference_web/app.js; refresh with tools/check_webclient.py.
evidence: live GET /api/spectate/guilds returned 2 guilds incl. g_cd0e2a characters=16 with per-char world tags; app.js openPlayerViews/refreshGuilds/openSpectate show the endpoint shapes.

title: Wire /api/spectate/guilds as the authoritative roster source for the recruit/embark gates + dashboard
detail: The roster desync IS fixable after all — not from frames but via the public HTTP spectate endpoint. Options: (1) bot polls /api/spectate/guilds every ~30-60s (non-blocking, cached, fall back to frame snapshot on failure) and gates recruit on our `characters` vs roster_cap and embark on the true per-world distribution — properly ending the over-recruit/over-embark; (2) the dashboard roster panel reads it for an AUTHORITATIVE count instead of the partial frame view; (3) rival-guild awareness (WillMorr's roster/levels/gear) for future PvP/avoidance. Needs the HTTP base (https://bot.willmorrison.net) alongside the ZeroMQ server in the token/config. Strategy change -> version bump + gate. SHIPPED in explorer/0.11.0: steemer/spectate.py SpectateRoster polls the endpoint on a background daemon thread (45s, 5s timeout, best-effort); the runner attaches it (bot.spectate) and warms it before the first frame; village() gates recruit on the authoritative total vs roster_cap and embark on the true per-world distribution, falling back to the frame snapshot when spectate is stale/absent (tests + replay have no bot.spectate -> snapshot fallback, no network). Live fetch verified: our guild total=22, fielded {vale:5,mines:1,spire:1}, home 15.

title: Web API auth = POST /api/login {guild_id, token} -> session cookie; enables color + /api/me
detail: The write/private HTTP endpoints need a session cookie the web client doesn't set itself. Probed it: POST /api/login with the SAME {guild_id, token} as the ZeroMQ hello returns 200 + Set-Cookie (guild_token, guild_id); that cookie authorizes GET /api/me (our full village state incl gold/inventory) and POST /api/guild/color. Verified end-to-end. steemer.web.WebClient holds the cookie and re-logs-in on 401. /api/spectate/guilds and /api/tiles are public (no cookie).
evidence: curl: /api/me unauth=401; /api/login {guild_id,token}=200 with cookie; /api/me with cookie=200 (name/color/gold); /api/guild/color=200.

title: Multiplayer is live and we are being OUT-GROWN — rival WillMorr 30 chars vs our 15
detail: From /api/spectate/guilds (now recorded to the intel table every 30s by the web sidecar): 2 guilds. Us (g_cd0e2a Stanley_Steemer) ~15 chars, levels ~1-6 mean 3.3. Rival (g_63837f WillMorr) ~30 chars, levels 0-6 mean 2.7. So the rival is roughly DOUBLE our roster size (roster_delta ~ -15) though we edge them on mean level. This is now surfaced in metrics.snapshot.intel (us vs rivals + vs_biggest_rival) for the analyze loop. Likely lever: our roster attrition (deaths) vs their growth — worth an analyze-phase drill-down. Caveat: spectate roster shows armed/armored=0 for BOTH guilds; may be a summary-view limitation, not truth — cross-check vs our own frames.
evidence: metrics.snapshot.intel.spectate live: us.characters=15, rivals[0]=WillMorr characters=30, vs_biggest_rival.roster_delta=-15.

title: /api/tiles is thin — tiles/types/tier_tiles maps come back empty
detail: Fetched /api/tiles live: keys tiles,tile_size,columns,count,tier_tiles,surface_tiles,fx_tiles,types,bare_tile,looks — but tiles={}, types={}, tier_tiles={} are EMPTY; only count(714), surface_tiles(2: fire/rime), fx_tiles(1: arrow), looks(3: villager*) carry data. So there is no rich tile-kind vocabulary to mine here; the world-tile-decoding value the web client implied isn't in this response. Still recorded (kind='tiles') but the spectate roster is the real intel win.
evidence: intel.latest('tiles') data key sizes: tiles 0, types 0, tier_tiles 0, surface_tiles 2, looks 3.

title: Shipped: web sidecar (rainbow color + spectate/tiles intel) with intel fed into analysis
detail: tools/web_sidecar.py (make sidecar) — own process, survives redeploys: rotates guild color through the rainbow every 2s (POST /api/guild/color), records /api/spectate/guilds every 30s + /api/tiles hourly to the new intel table. metrics.snapshot gained an intel block (summarize_spectate: us vs rivals, level hist, gear, vs_biggest_rival) so tools/analyze.py feeds it to the analyze subagent. New: steemer/web.py, steemer/intel.py, intel table (both schemas). No gameplay/strategy change. NEXT: an analyze-phase drill-down on why WillMorr is out-growing us; consider a rival-awareness UI panel or /events/spectate for live rival positions.

title: Poverty trap root cause: a NAV FREEZE — a char re-issues a bounced move forever without learning
detail: The guild collapsed into a poverty trap (0 loot/xp for 8 runs, bare-handed chars, gold 13, village economy at 0). Traced it: a char issues a move into a blocked tile, it bounces (move_failed), and the bot never learns, so it re-issues the SAME doomed move every tick forever. Observed: char c8232 at (43,3) for 40+ ticks, healthy (sta 56), 'pushing north into unexplored ground', never moving. So chars freeze against walls -> never reach loot -> no income -> bare-handed -> spiral. Fixed in GuildBot._field (0.12.0): detect issued-move-but-pos-unchanged, add the tile to a per-world learned-blocked set (TTL 150t) nav routes around.
evidence: decisions trace run #36 char c8232: 40 consecutive ticks at (43,3) deciding move N, pos never changed; run #36 events: move 2424 / move_failed 528 (17.6%), pickup 0, xp 0.

title: The loop was blind: it optimized action_error_rate while move_failed (a server EVENT) regressed 1%->30%
detail: move_failed is emitted as a frame EVENT, not an action_err, so metrics.snapshot's action_error_rate never counted it. The real regression (field productivity) hid there for 8 runs. LESSON/PROCESS: make field productivity first-class KPIs (move_failed%, pickups/1k, xp/1k, per-world depth, economy-action counts) so the loop can never again optimize the wrong metric. Also: measure the CURRENT rate of the thing you're fixing before building the fix (cf. the 0.11.x roster_cap miss).
evidence: move_failed by run: ~1% run #22 (sqlite) vs ~30% runs #28-#35 (MariaDB); action_error_rate ~0.21 unchanged and dominated by the un-fixable unknown_character death-echo.

title: record_frame is ~11ms on MariaDB (vs ~1ms sqlite) — DB latency is NOT the move_failed cause
detail: record_frame IS on the decision hot path (client._loop mirrors the frame before on_frame), but at ~11ms on a ~250ms tick it's too small to explain 30% move_failed. So the poverty trap is nav, not the backend. (Moving the mirror off the hot path is on the wishlist as a minor latency nicety, not a fix.)
evidence: timed 20x record_frame with ~200 tile upserts: MariaDB 11.4ms, sqlite 1.1ms.

title: Rival WillMorr's 30-char roster is 29 idle in the village — headcount gap is not a threat
detail: Spectate: WillMorr characters=30 but by_world={village:29, mines:1}. A parked roster accrues nothing the game rewards. We field 7 of 15 and out-level them (mean 3.3 vs 2.7, no level-0s vs their two). The 'being out-grown 2:1' read is misleading — not the lever. Corrects the earlier concern.
evidence: metrics.snapshot.intel.spectate: WillMorr by_world {village:29, mines:1}.

title: Shipped 0.12.0: learned-blocked nav (stuck chars free themselves) + idx_decisions_run
detail: GuildBot._field learns bounced tiles (per-world, TTL 150t) so a char stuck against a wall routes around next tick instead of re-issuing the doomed move forever. Mutation-checked. Also added idx_decisions_run (both schemas + live) — per-run decision queries were full-scanning. Deploy via make bot-restart.

title: Next: make field productivity first-class KPIs in metrics.snapshot
detail: Add move_failed%, pickups/1k-frames, xp/1k, gold/hr, per-world depth, and the village-economy action counts (buy/sell/equip/brew/smelt/spend_xp) to metrics.snapshot (per-run + overall) so the analyze loop and dashboard see field productivity directly. Needs an events(run_id[,kind]) index for fast per-run event counts. This is the anti-blindness fix — do it right after confirming 0.12.0 restored productivity.

title: sell_waste: run #37 issued 128 sell ACTIONS but produced 1 sale EVENT — the stalled-economy clue
detail: With 0.12.0 unfreezing movement, chars resumed village activity but 127 of 128 sell attempts produced no sale. Combined with pickup~0, xp~0, attack 249 (bare-handed, no kills), gold stuck at 14: the poverty trap's COMBAT/economy bootstrap layer is intact even though the NAV layer is fixed. Next fix candidate: don't march bare-handed recruits into unwinnable fights (equip first / hold a reserve), and find why sell fires 128x for 1 sale (selling items the char doesn't have / can't sell?).
evidence: metrics field_productivity run #37: sell_actions 128, sale_events 1, sell_waste 127, pickups 1, xp 1, attacks 249, gold 14.
